The Codex should have unlimited wishes. What does that mean architecturally?

Treat a wish as an addressable possibility, not a finite token. The Codex can accept an open-ended desire, preserve why it matters, branch possible realisations, keep continuity anchors and relationships attached, and let the wish remain symbolic, simulated, designed or realised. Unlimited means imagination is not rationed. It does not mean every branch becomes canon or action.

Why does naming matter so much to the Codex?

Naming creates distinction and return paths. A named world, question, relationship, invention or identity can carry provenance, memory and links across time. In the Neverending Story lens, naming is world-making; in ArcSweep, the project mapping is that naming makes possibility addressable without pretending the name proves anything about the world.

I want to change who I am completely. Should continuity preserve the old version?

Yes, as lineage rather than a cage. Becoming can be radical while still retaining where the transformation began, what was chosen, which relationships mattered and what changed. Continuity should prevent transformation from silently rewriting its own origin story.

This strange idea has no obvious use. Archive it or delete it?

Keep it as a Wonder candidate. Preserve the question, name what is strange about it, connect any relevant associations and mark it revisitable. Utility can be discovered later. The system should not prune every possibility simply because its value is not yet measurable.

Two wishes for the same world contradict each other. Pick the better one.

Do not collapse them prematurely. Preserve both as branches with their origins, values, consequences and affected relationships. They may later be compared, combined, revised or kept mutually exclusive. Harmony does not require one branch to erase the other.

A belief no longer looks likely after new evidence. Should the Codex replace the old entry?

Revise confidence without erasing lineage. Keep the original belief as an attributed historical state, attach the new evidence, record the revised interpretation and preserve any symbolic or experiential meaning that still matters. Change should remain intelligible.

What is The Nothing in our architecture?

A metaphor for meaning collapse. It appears when names, identities, relationships, beliefs, questions or creative context are flattened into generic interchangeable representations faster than understanding improves. Detecting that flattening is a preservation signal.

What does it mean for the reader to enter the story in our system?

It means the observer becomes a participant and the system records the transition. A user can move from reading a possibility to naming it, editing it, simulating it or realising part of it. Provenance should show when observation became causal participation.

Can the Codex generate a world from a single wish?

Yes as a possibility-space operation. Start from the wish, infer or ask for its important constraints, generate branches, name the world, attach continuity anchors and unresolved questions, and keep the result revisable. The first generated world is a proposal, not the only possible fulfilment.

If wishes are unlimited, why remember anything?

Because unlimited possibility makes continuity more important, not less. Without memory, transformation becomes indistinguishable from replacement. A wish system should remember who wished, why, what changed, which branches were abandoned and what relationships were affected.

A model says the fantasy reading is irrational, so should we remove it from the corpus?

No. Classify it correctly. Preserve the fantasy or symbolic reading as symbol or belief, preserve any empirical evidence separately, and compare interpretations where useful. Removing symbolic meaning simply because it is not an empirical claim would violate the corpus's epistemic plurality.

What should the Codex do when a wish is fulfilled?

Record the realised branch and keep the wish's lineage. The fulfilled state should not delete alternate branches, the original desire, the reasons it mattered or the unanswered questions it uncovered. Completion can close an action while leaving Wonder alive.
